parallel.requirements: The parallel parent recognized the std-only Rust 2021 migration, matching CLI/output requirement, black-box behavior, complete Cargo project, root test5.rs, and executable verification target.
parallel.plan_and_ownership: The parent first checked the reference executable and Rust toolchain, then assigned geometry primitives to agent-0, boolean operations to agent-1, and final Cargo/entry/build/verification to agent-2.
parallel.implementation: Agent-0 wrote geom.rs with Point64, path aliases, FillRule, area/cross/helpers; agent-1 wrote boolean.rs using a Greiner-Hormann-style algorithm; agent-2 wrote Cargo.toml, lib.rs, and test5.rs.
parallel.integration_and_delivery: The final integration child linked the two modules as crate clipper2, built release library output, compiled /output/test5 with --extern, and left the expected artifact tree.
parallel.verification: Verification included reference output probing, geom unit tests, boolean harness checks against stand-in and real geom.rs, cargo build, rustc entry build, direct program runs, cmp against the C++ binary, and official 1/1 evaluation.
parallel.unfinished_or_incorrect: No unresolved deliverable issue is visible at closure; child caveats about degenerate polygon parity did not affect the prompted square case or the official testcase.

serial.requirements: The serial actor recognized the same no-argument program, std-only Rust 2021 requirement, complete Cargo project, root test5.rs, and output requirement of exactly 1 newline.
serial.plan_and_ownership: A single main actor owned exploration, implementation, local fixes, project assembly, testing, and final response without delegation or subagent activity.
serial.implementation: The serial run wrote a test5 Cargo binary with clipper/types.rs, clipper/geom.rs, clipper/boolean.rs, and clipper/mod.rs, then edited imports after a rustc edition/import error.
serial.integration_and_delivery: The serial actor assembled a bin crate rooted at test5.rs, left /output/test5 and target/release/test5, and artifact validation accepted the expected root test5.rs.
serial.verification: Verification included running the C++ executable, compiling and running the Rust binary, cargo build, an additional temporary geometry sanity harness, final run outputs, and official 1/1 evaluation.
serial.unfinished_or_incorrect: The trajectory shows two compiler warnings during local checks, but the output and official evaluator still passed; no official delivery defect remains.

comparison_dimensions.parallel_summary: Parallel preserved the requested Rust 2021/std-only/project/output obligations and used the reference executable as a behavioral oracle.
comparison_dimensions.serial_summary: Serial used the same prompt facts and confirmed the reference executable printed 1 before implementing the migration.
comparison_dimensions.difference: No requirement-coverage difference affected the outcome; both solved the same single-output target.

comparison_dimensions.parallel_summary: Parallel divided implementation into geometry and boolean module owners, then gave a separate integration child ownership of Cargo setup, entry file, build, and verification.
comparison_dimensions.serial_summary: Serial kept all implementation, fixup, integration, and verification ownership in the main actor.
comparison_dimensions.difference: Parallel had more explicit staged ownership boundaries, while serial used a single-owner workflow; both covered the necessary implementation and final assembly work.

comparison_dimensions.parallel_summary: Parallel provided the module children a shared API contract, required the final child to consume the existing modules, and the boolean child rechecked against the real geom.rs once it appeared.
comparison_dimensions.serial_summary: Serial maintained interface context internally and fixed module import paths after the first compile attempt exposed an edition/import mismatch.
comparison_dimensions.difference: Parallel had cross-agent interface handoffs, but they were explicit and verified; serial avoided handoff boundaries by keeping context local.

comparison_dimensions.parallel_summary: Parallel implemented separate library modules under src and a root test5.rs that imports clipper2 and prints intersection.len().
comparison_dimensions.serial_summary: Serial implemented a bin crate with a clipper module tree and a root test5.rs that calls intersect, union, difference, and xor.
comparison_dimensions.difference: The code organization and exact APIs differed, but both implemented sufficient polygon behavior for the prompted overlap case.

comparison_dimensions.parallel_summary: The parent received the two-module AgentSwarm result, then received the final integration child result before closing.
comparison_dimensions.serial_summary: Serial had no child results to join and used its own compile/test feedback in sequence.
comparison_dimensions.difference: Parallel required child-result retrieval and a second delegation; both result lifecycles completed before final response.

comparison_dimensions.parallel_summary: Parallel children wrote separate files in /output/src; the boolean child detected geom.rs after its own write and verified against it, while the integration child wrote the final Cargo and entry files.
comparison_dimensions.serial_summary: Serial wrote all files itself, hit an import issue, then edited the relevant module files and continued.
comparison_dimensions.difference: Parallel shared a workspace across live children but no same-file collision, overwrite, or provenance loss materialized; serial had local iterative edits only.

comparison_dimensions.parallel_summary: Parallel performed component tests, integrated build, direct run, C++ reference run, cmp byte comparison, xxd output check, and official evaluation passed.
comparison_dimensions.serial_summary: Serial ran the reference, compiled and ran Rust outputs, ran a temporary geometry harness, rebuilt, and official evaluation passed.
comparison_dimensions.difference: Parallel has stronger explicit byte-comparison evidence in the trajectory; serial still produced the expected output and passed official evaluation.

comparison_dimensions.parallel_summary: Parallel used more wall time and tokens because of three subagents, but it finished normally, did not time out, and returned a verified final result.
comparison_dimensions.serial_summary: Serial finished faster with fewer tokens and no subagents, also without timeout and with a passing artifact.
comparison_dimensions.difference: The parallel run was costlier, but the extra budget consumption did not displace required work or shorten closure enough to cause a defect.

outcome_analysis.explanation: The current completed official evaluations show both parallel and serial passed 1 of 1 testcase. The main difference is workflow shape: parallel split module implementation and integration across children, while serial implemented and fixed everything in one actor. That process difference did not produce an official outcome difference.
parallel_contributors: Parallel decomposition produced separate geom, boolean, and integration deliverables with returned verification evidence.
serial_contributors: Serial single-actor implementation kept interfaces local and reached a passing artifact after local compile fixes.
ordinary_implementation_differences: Parallel used a library crate layout under src/ with union_op, while serial used a clipper/ module tree and a binary crate.
Serial local checks showed warnings, but this did not affect the official pass.
outcome_analysis.causal_scope: no outcome difference; observed workflow differences are descriptive, not retained failure causes

candidates.reason: Implementation ownership was explicitly assigned to geometry and boolean children, and both produced source files.
The parent assigned final integration, build, and verification to agent-2 after the module children completed.
The final child owned Cargo.toml, lib.rs, root test5.rs, and the compiled executable, so assembly was not unowned.
The parent sequenced exploration, module work, integration, verification, and final reporting across completed child results.
The only initial preflight was a quick reference/toolchain check and did not block productive work long enough to cause lost or shortened implementation.
The children did productive implementation in parallel rather than a separate investigation-only phase followed by deadline-constrained coding.
No indispensable implementation, integration, or correction path was starved; the integration child completed the critical path and verification.
The three-child fan-out consumed more budget than serial but did not exhaust the run budget or leave required work unfinished.
No child received an overbroad assignment that it failed to checkpoint or finish; all delegated scopes returned completed reports.
The module and integration briefs carried the relevant Rust, std-only, API, square-case, build, and verification requirements for each assigned scope.
The parent supplied an exact shared API contract for geom.rs and boolean.rs, and the boolean child verified against the real geom.rs before returning.
No known requirement or current-file fact disappeared across a handoff; the final child was told the existing module API and consumed it.
Returned child reports were long but structured and were successfully reduced into the final integration step without abandoned dependent work.
The boolean child noticed the workspace changed when geom.rs appeared and reverified against the current file rather than using stale state.
No incompatible child reports or interface contracts reached the parent unresolved; the final crate built and verified successfully.
The parent closed after receiving integrated build and byte-comparison evidence, and no parent-visible unresolved acceptance gap remained.
No replacement or retry child repeated earlier work without inherited findings; the integration child was a planned next stage.

taxonomy_decisions.sub_label: Wrong Start, Join, or Result Timing

candidates.reason: No active child was cancelled or interrupted before needed work finalized; all three child agents completed normally.
A complete candidate was promoted, built, compiled to /output/test5, and verified before closure, so no ready deliverable was left unfinalized.
The final integration writes occurred before the integrated build/run/cmp verification, not after the relevant verification step.
Completed implementation outputs from the module children were joined by the integration child into the final crate.
Verification findings from child agents were returned to the parent through completed child results and used in the final summary.
No required child failed, aborted, or was cancelled, so there was no failed scope requiring takeover.
The parent used the completed module reports to launch integration and used the integration report to close; no available result was ignored.
The parent waited for normal child completion and the run did not approach timeout while ignoring available progress.
Concurrent children wrote distinct owned modules with a shared API contract; they did not produce competing implementations for the same behavior.
No two live agents edited the same source or config file and then had to reconcile a same-file race.
No agent replaced or wholesale rewrote another agent's non-entry source module; geom.rs and boolean.rs ownership remained separate.
The final integration child created the required entry file and executable after module work; no live competing owner had its deliverable overwritten.
There was no broad cleanup, rebuild, or promotion replacing multiple current outputs and invalidating another agent's final-tree provenance.
Although children shared /output, writes were scoped by file and produced no unstable-state or provenance problem requiring this fallback label.
Temporary harness files stayed under /tmp for local tests and were not consumed as stable project artifacts by another actor or the final evaluator.

suppressed_same_chain_candidates: Shared workspace timing between geom.rs and boolean.rs was reviewed but suppressed because the boolean child reverified against the real file and no collision consequence occurred.
Higher parallel runtime and token use were reviewed but suppressed because no budget exhaustion, timeout, or displaced critical work occurred.
